sections.overview: Lyons' cichlid is a freshwater fish of the Cichlidae, restricted to the Pacific slope of southern Costa Rica and western Panama. Its range is small and scattered across river basins.
sections.identification: Adults show seven dark bars and about eight flank blotches, often edged in turquoise, over grey-brown, green-brown or yellowish sides. The Spanish key distinguishes it from the thick-lipped Amphilophus labiatus by its less prominent lips, shorter pectoral fin and diffuse bars. Females have a dark spot at the dorsal-fin base. FishBase gives 15 cm standard length; at that length the study’s body proportions imply 5.6–7.5 cm depth and 2.6–3.1 cm width, while its mass model estimates about 130 g, without a sex-specific range.
sections.habitat: It lives in lowland rivers and ponds with sandy or silty bottoms and moderate to very slow current. Verified sites are warm, around 26–29 °C, in southern Costa Rica and western Panama.
sections.diet: It eats seeds, aquatic and terrestrial insects, crustaceans and bottom detritus. A 2022 stomach-content sample of only two preserved fish was dominated by aquatic insects and detritus, so those proportions are indicative, not a broad diet estimate.
sections.behavior: Both parents tend and fan the eggs, guard young, and carry newly hatched fry to pits excavated in the substrate, often in dark cavities.
sections.reproduction: Eggs are laid on cleaned rocks or branches, usually once or twice yearly and occasionally up to six times; clutch size is not reliably recorded.
sections.ecology: Rediscovered in Costa Rica in 2022 after no verified records there since 1973, it was found at three of 15 surveyed sites and described as rare to locally uncommon.
sections.conservation: The IUCN lists it as Endangered (EN), assessed in 2019: its estimated range is about 2,077 km² and includes fewer than five locations. The assessment identifies deforestation, agricultural pollution and river dredging as pressures on habitat; population size remains unknown.
